body: Can you paste the SQL? I don't understand how adding a ORDER BY to a count can result in a SQL error.

SQL query before cake update:

``` sql
SELECT (COUNT(*)) AS "count" FROM "offers"."generic_products_details" "GenericProductsDetails" WHERE "product_id" = 4
```

And now:

``` sql
SELECT (COUNT(*)) AS "count" FROM "offers"."generic_products_details" "GenericProductsDetails" WHERE "product_id" = $1 ORDER BY "GenericProductsDetails"."price" ASC
```
Where is the order by in that query?
I updated generated query. Previous was before cake update.

@lorenzo I actually had this exact same issue the other day, though I was doing something wrong and moved on. Apparently it wasn't just me.

So, essentially, SQL Server (And probably some others) does not allow you to order by a field that is not grouped if you are doing an aggregate.
So

``` SQL
SELECT field_name FROM table ORDER BY field_name2 ASC
```

is valid, but

``` SQL
SELECT count(*) FROM table ORDER BY field_name2 ASC
```

gives `[2014-11-13 11:17:59] [S0001][8127] Column "field_name2" is invalid in the ORDER BY clause because it is not contained in either an aggregate function or the GROUP BY clause.`

Usually, doing `$query->order(['field' => 'ASC'])->count()` will remove the order field as part of the `count()` method.

The particular issue here stems from the moving of the Model.beforeFind event to be fired in the `Query::Sql()` method, which in the case of a `count()` will be called after the order by clause is removed from the original query. So if you add a default order by in your beforeFind, any `count()` will cause this error.

Yeah, I know what changed to trigger this error. Just a bit surprised this would be invalid SQL for some databases. Currently I'm completely out of ideas how to solve that, other than informing callbacks "this is a count", but I'm not happy with that.

I think its not good if query count sometimes skip order by, sometimes doesn't. I'm not so familiar with query builder, but I think that problem should be solved in query builder, not just inform callback methods "watch out, its query count"

issue.body:
As reported in #5150, some databases don't like including `order by` along with `count(*)`, this is usually not a problem as the `Query::count()` method creates a clean copy of the query which excludes any counts or limits. However, if the query is modified in the beforeFind callback, the count() method will not clean up any added parts.

This PR corrects that issue by triggering beforeFind as part of the clean-up process.
